title: Smell Reads Patterns, Taste Reads Cells

scenes.tts: Smell and taste both detect chemicals. Why do they read them so differently? In a mouse, most mature olfactory neurons express one receptor gene at high abundance, chosen from roughly a thousand. That is a statement about genes, not about odorants. One receptor can still bind many odorants.
scenes.visual: Two chips, smell and taste, with a question mark; then a grid of receptor genes, one picked into an olfactory neuron's cilia, and several odorants binding that one receptor.
scenes.narration: Smell and taste both detect chemicals. Why do they read them so differently? In a mouse, most mature olfactory neurons express one receptor gene at high abundance, chosen from roughly a thousand. That is a statement about genes, not about odorants. One receptor can still bind many odorants.

scenes.tts: Where do their axons go? In mice, axons from neurons that share one receptor start scattered across the olfactory epithelium. They converge on two fixed glomeruli in each olfactory bulb. So each glomerulus collects mainly from one receptor type. The glomerular layer is largely a map of receptor identity.
scenes.visual: Scattered neurons in the epithelium, those sharing one receptor turn blue and their axons gather onto two glomeruli of the bulb, which fill blue.

scenes.tts: Here is an invented example with four receptors, A to D. Odorant two activates B and C. Odorant three activates A, B and C. Imaging of mouse olfactory neurons found the same two things. One receptor recognized several odorants. One odorant was recognized by several receptors.
scenes.visual: A receptor by odorant matrix fills row by row; column B is boxed, then row three is boxed.
scenes.narration: Here is an invented example with four receptors, A to D. Odorant two activates B and C. Odorant three activates A, B and C. Imaging of mouse olfactory neurons found the same two things. One receptor recognized several odorants. One odorant was recognized by several receptors.

scenes.tts: Now remove receptor A. Odorant two still gives B and C. Odorant three now gives B and C as well. The model predicts they can no longer be told apart. Odorant one activates A and B. At tenfold concentration it also recruits receptor C, a lower-affinity receptor. Its pattern now matches odorant three. The model predicts it could be mistaken for odorant three. This is a toy model, not a count of smells.
scenes.visual: Column A is crossed out and odorant three's pattern collapses onto odorant two's; then A is restored, odorant one is added and gains C at tenfold concentration, matching odorant three.
scenes.narration: Now remove receptor A. Odorant two still gives B and C. Odorant three now gives B and C as well. The model predicts they can no longer be told apart. Odorant one activates A and B. scenes.tts: Taste works differently. In mouse taste buds, sweet, umami and bitter cells carry different receptors. After the receptor, they share the same steps, including the enzyme P L C beta two. If the machinery is shared, what keeps sweet and bitter apart? Zhang and colleagues removed P L C beta two. The tested sweet, amino acid and bitter responses were lost. Sour and salty responses were spared.
scenes.visual: Three taste cells with their own receptors share one PLCβ2 chip each; PLCβ2 is crossed out and the three lamps go dark while sour and salty cells stay lit.
scenes.caption: Taste works differently. In mouse taste buds, sweet, umami and bitter cells carry different receptors. After the receptor, they share the same steps, including the enzyme PLCβ2. If the machinery is shared, what keeps sweet and bitter apart? Zhang and colleagues removed PLCβ2. The tested sweet, amino acid and bitter responses were lost. Sour and salty responses were spared.
scenes.narration: Taste works differently. In mouse taste buds, sweet, umami and bitter cells carry different receptors. After the receptor, they share the same steps, including the enzyme PLCβ2. If the machinery is shared, what keeps sweet and bitter apart? Zhang and colleagues removed PLCβ2. The tested sweet, amino acid and bitter responses were lost. Sour and salty responses were spared.

scenes.tts: Then they restored P L C beta two only in cells that express bitter receptors. Bitter responses returned. Sweet and amino acid responses did not. The shared cascade carried whichever quality its cell was wired to report. These are mouse experiments on the periphery. Smell reads a pattern. Taste reads which cell fires.
scenes.visual: PLCβ2 comes back in the bitter cell only and only the bitter lamp relights; then a final split shows smell as a pattern across receptors and taste as one cell firing.
